anchors.paper_title: EEG Signatures of COVID-19 Survival compared to close contacts and the Cuban EEG normative database
anchors.reason: The paper title and abstract specifically analyze and report findings using the 173 participants (87 COVID-19 cases, 86 close contacts) and the Cuban EEG normative database, which constitute this dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was acquired using a 10-20 standard montage. Resting EEG was recorded for 8 minutes with eyes closed in all participants. Additional recordings included 2 minutes of alternating closed and open eyes, followed by 2 minutes of recovery.

funding.funder_name: National Key R&D Program of China

citation_details.title: A COVID-19 survivors and close contacts EEG dataset
citation_details.author: Ana Calzada-Reyes, Eduardo Aubert-Vázquez, Lidice Galán-García, Maria Luisa Bringas-Vega, Trinidad Virués-Alba, Lidia Charroó-Ruiz, Yanely Acosta-Imas, Mitchell Valdés-Sosa, Laura Perez-Mayo, Joel Gutiérrez-Gil, Antonio Caballero-Moreno, Miguel Angel Alvarez, Norge Santiesteban, Javier Vicente Sánchez-Lopez, Annette Valdés-Virués, Elba Elvira Varona-Galindo, Elizabeth Méndez‐Parra, Joviana Castro-Valiente, Leyanis Ramos-Hernández, Mabel Whilby-Santiesteban, Thelma Luz Carrillo-Alfonso, Shahwar Yasir, Yu Kin, Peng Ren, Dezhong Yao, Luo Cheng, Roberto Rodríguez-Labrada, Pedro Valdés-Sosa
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises 169 resting-state electroencephalograms (EEGs) from COVID-19 survivors (n=86) and close contacts/healthy controls (n=83), acquired using standard 10-20 electrode montage. The study investigates neurophysiological signatures of COVID-19 infection through quantitative EEG analysis, comparing spectral and functional connectivity patterns between groups and against a Cuban normative database. The dataset includes 8 minutes of eyes-closed resting EEG, followed by alternating eye-state conditions, providing a comprehensive neurophysiological characterization of post-COVID neurological sequelae.
